What the market research showed

  • Most fundraising advisors charge a monthly retainer plus a success fee of roughly 1% to 3% of the capital actually raised. Others charge more, with retainers of about $5K to $25K+ per month for 3 to 6 months and success fees of 2% to 8%.
  • Many focus on later rounds, usually from Series A onward.
  • Global life-science advisors bring real science depth, but they mostly serve VC firms, private equity funds and asset managers out of London and Cambridge, MA.
  • Founders' most common worry is paying upfront for investor access with vague deliverables.
  • For deep-tech founders the real gap is commercialisation. As a 2026 panel put it, without a business behind the engineering, the venture stays a side project.

About me

I am an award-winning innovation and ecosystem development professional with more than two years in the startup and biotechnology ecosystem, based in Bengaluru.

I was recognised with the Best Summer Internship Project Award (2025) among a cohort of 1,500 students at BIRAC. My strengths are startup research and data analysis, guiding early-stage ventures through incubation, funding and commercialisation, and streamlining funding decisions so technology-led ventures are better prepared for the market.
